projects.title: Turnkeep
projects.descriptor: A character case for the tabletop
projects.summary: I designed Turnkeep to bring the game back to the table: a character case that combines storage, a small display and tactile controls for tabletop play. The public prototype includes editable CAD, printable parts, firmware and build instructions so other makers can adapt it. It is a project about making things for the hobbies I love, with the next stages still being tested and developed.

projects.title: Reggio projects
projects.descriptor: A decade of questions made tangible
projects.summary: Over the past decade, my educational work has brought materials, electronics and open-ended questions into children's project work. This selection gathers the provocations, prototypes and documentation I have designed or co-facilitated, from Arduino explorations to a Year 6 AI sprint. The objects matter, but so does the record of how ideas changed while children made, tested and discussed them.

projects.title: Padlano
projects.summary: I built Padlano to make a casual padel session easier to run from one phone. It creates Americano rotations, tracks scores and ranks players fairly when someone sits out a round. The app is free to use without an account, with data stored locally unless players choose to share a session or league. It grew from wanting less administration between games and more time on court.

projects.title: A school for making
projects.descriptor: An alternative middle school & community maker space
projects.summary: I am developing a model for an alternative middle school and community maker space where practical projects connect learning with the world outside the classroom. The work brings programme design, tools and spaces together, considering how young people can investigate ideas, build things and learn alongside others. This case presents the concept and design work in progress, rather than an operating school.

projects.title: ELC Portal
projects.descriptor: A clearer front door to school life
projects.summary: I designed and built a family-facing portal to make school life easier to navigate beyond the classroom. It brings activities, events, calendars and useful information into a consistent front door, while connecting families to the school's existing registration systems. The work combines experience design with practical school operations: helping people find the next thing they need without having to understand the systems behind it.

projects.title: Pomodoist
projects.descriptor: One small screen. One thing at a time.
projects.summary: Pomodoist is my experiment in giving focused work a small physical interface. It brings a Pomodoro timer and Todoist tasks onto ESP32 devices, separating the shared timer logic from the screen and controls of each board. I am exploring how a dedicated object can keep one task in view without adding another full computer interface to the desk.

projects.title: Project dashboard
projects.descriptor: A little structure for shared work
projects.summary: I turned an internal project-management tool into a public single-file dashboard template. It brings priorities, progress and weekly updates into one place, with browser-based storage and an optional shareable view. The aim was to make a useful working tool that someone could adapt and host without setting up a server or committing to another subscription.

projects.title: ESP32 experiments
projects.summary: My ESP32 work explores how useful little devices can share the same underlying software. Timers, scoreboards and desk displays become different faces for portable app logic, with each board contributing its own screen, controls and physical constraints. This is an ongoing collection of firmware, interface and hardware experiments, built to learn from and reuse across the things I make.

projects.title: Second Brain Builder
projects.summary: I made Second Brain Builder to help friends shape a knowledge system around their own work and habits. Each personalised build guides someone through questions about how they think, plan and keep track of things, then creates a plain-text blueprint for an AI-assisted workspace. It turns the structure behind my own second brain into something another person can make their own.

projects.title: Trips
projects.descriptor: Custom apps for friends and loved ones
projects.summary: I make small, custom apps for friends and loved ones. Trips brings a shared day out into one easy-to-use guide: places to stop, the story behind each one, practical details and a checklist that stays in sync. Built as installable web pages with offline access, it puts the plan in everyone’s pocket and leaves room to enjoy the day together.
